verdict.rationale: AnythingLLM's own docs say it is a private assistant that runs entirely on your computer, with no accounts or API keys. Hands-on community reports back this up: Ollama is detected automatically, and one user calls it an offline AI tool. Because the story lists backends as alternatives, Ollama support covers its core. Missing for 10: first-party docs naming supported local backends (LM Studio and vLLM are never mentioned, llama.cpp only in a commenter's aside), explicit documentation that no cloud call is needed for chat inference.

support.subject: As a privacy-first user, I can run the assistant entirely on local models — Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, or vLLM — with no cloud model dependency

citations.quote: A private AI assistant that runs entirely on your computer. No accounts, no API keys, no token limits.
With Ollama, everything was automatically detected, while manual setup is still possible.
this has been the only offline AI tool I've been able to install and start using on my standard office PC.
get a privacy-focused, extensible, and capable AI agent running on your device in minutes.
